reasons: The accepted landscape covers four substantively different mechanism families with active, analyzed primary-paper representatives: token-selective retention, low-bit representation, trained head/layer sharing, and exact-or-encoded serving memory management/reuse/hierarchy.

The fifteen sourced cross-paper findings cover the KV bottleneck, which resource each route reduces, quality/latency/throughput/memory and hardware/kernel tradeoffs, inference-only versus training-time deployment boundaries, conditional composition, limitations, and a concrete literature disagreement.

Four sourced open problems cover unresolved quality adaptation, portable extreme quantization, large-model architectural validation and composition, and joint serving control; no accepted investigation gap remains open.

Stable-ref inspection found fourteen active analyzed papers, and targeted primary-source reads independently confirmed the network-transfer distinction, the missing end-to-end serving validation for cross-layer sharing, and the demonstrated non-plug-and-play behavior of eviction-plus-INT2 composition.
The accepted evidence is sufficient for the required mechanism-organized Chinese survey; remaining work is delivery synthesis and citation rendering rather than additional research.
check_d8e26b18-81df-4d64-b859-4d367b1442.requester_rationale: The adaptive research loop has resolved all four investigation gaps and now covers the contract through four mechanism-level routes, current-run primary-paper analyses, cross-paper findings, and grounded open problems.

deliverable.description: 一份中文 KV Cache 优化技术路线 Survey，覆盖主要路线、代表论文、机制、方法比较、工程权衡、路线关系、limitations、open problems 与可追溯引用。

contract.mission: 理解 LLM inference 中 KV Cache 优化的主要技术路线，以及不同路线如何在 memory、latency、throughput、quality 与部署复杂度之间进行权衡。

requirement_29ae7bcc-1884-4ccb-a17e-6398.statement: 明确当前文献中的重要 limitation 与 disagreement。

requirement_380f214b-5ba9-455c-bd9d-3be2.statement: 形成按技术机制和路线组织、而不是按论文排列的中文领域 Survey。

requirement_43fd81a5-cfa5-41d9-a9ef-b5b2.statement: 解释 KV Cache 为什么成为长上下文和高并发 LLM inference 的关键瓶颈。

requirement_6bf430d1-bca5-4dee-b7ef-0a61.statement: 总结有文献依据的 open problems。

requirement_739574d0-1234-439b-b0f1-2532.statement: 比较不同路线主要减少的 memory footprint、bandwidth、transfer cost、compute 与 serving pressure。

requirement_94c24a84-efda-49fb-af02-cbe7.statement: 区分 inference-only 方法与需要训练、finetuning 或 architectural modification 的方法。

requirement_94f53018-fc09-4177-a5ea-77d0.statement: 为每条主要路线提供真实 Primary Papers。

requirement_bb01a139-2ccd-4f72-9ac4-651a.statement: 讨论不同 KV Cache 优化路线之间是否可以组合。

requirement_bdec21f5-00c1-4e5e-a26a-9c7e.statement: 识别主要且有实质机制差异的 KV Cache 优化技术路线。

requirement_d3d18dc5-5248-4b15-aae3-1b95.statement: 比较 quality degradation、latency、throughput、memory saving、implementation complexity 与 hardware dependence。

contract.scope: 聚焦 Transformer/LLM inference-time KV Cache；主要使用 DeepXiv 可发现、可访问的 arXiv Primary Papers。Survey 仅作 discovery lead，不作主要 proof；不扩展为所有 serving optimization，general model quantization、weight pruning 与 speculative decoding 仅在直接涉及 KV Cache 时纳入。

gap_0597a4b8-8903-4422-b74e-d394f727bfd4.description: Layer/head-adaptive hybrid evidence remains weak: analyze XKV and MiniKV and determine whether budget allocation plus eviction/quantization forms a distinct route or a combination strategy.
gap_0597a4b8-8903-4422-b74e-d394f727bfd4.resolution: Resolved by analyzing XKV and MiniKV. Layer-adaptive budgets are classified as a policy inside token selection, while MiniKV is an explicit selection-plus-INT2 composition. New findings capture calibration costs, medium-budget assumptions, kernel co-design, and the failed SnapKV-plus-KIVI composition.

gap_09b27824-b2ab-4b3b-a68f-2497425c6187.description: The architecture-changing route is retained but not yet analyzed: read CLA, MLKV, and bounded-cache Transformer to distinguish head/layer sharing and trained bounded state from inference-only compression.
gap_09b27824-b2ab-4b3b-a68f-2497425c6187.resolution: Resolved by analyzing CLA and MLKV and adding the architectural head/layer-sharing family. Both require training or uptraining and reduce distinct KV tensors, unlike inference-only compression; both also show that cache capacity reduction need not reduce per-layer bandwidth. The predefined-capacity paper was analyzed but retired because its method and results are not sufficiently specified for representative use.

gap_95549d7e-02c6-48f8-b2ae-aa4f6398da23.description: Current primary papers underrepresent reasoning and long-generation failure modes of cache compression; perform a targeted follow-up search and verify at least one independent limitation study or challenging benchmark.
gap_95549d7e-02c6-48f8-b2ae-aa4f6398da23.resolution: Resolved through two targeted, independent primary evaluations: Hold Onto That Thought tests up to 2048 generated reasoning tokens and identifies accuracy collapse, longer traces, and nontermination at small budgets; KVFundaBench covers six capabilities and roughly 4K-token generation, showing task-, model-, prompt-, and policy-specific degradation and a material disagreement about reasoning-model robustness.

gap_c572bedb-1c96-4de5-bcc7-b09c86f2578a.description: Serving-level reuse and offloading evidence is thin: analyze LMCache and search for representative paged/prefix-cache or heterogeneous-memory primary work before generalizing the memory-hierarchy route.
gap_c572bedb-1c96-4de5-bcc7-b09c86f2578a.resolution: Resolved by targeted DeepXiv discovery and analysis of PagedAttention/vLLM plus LMCache. The memory-hierarchy family now distinguishes exact paged allocation/prefix sharing, heterogeneous exact reuse/offload, and CacheGen's encoded transfer; findings record their workload, bandwidth, and hit-rate conditions.

approach_1aa1ad25-f3d9-4369-ae7f-7eaad31.core_idea: Preserve exact or encoded KV state while eliminating allocation waste, sharing common prefixes, avoiding repeated prefill, and moving cache through GPU/CPU/disk/network tiers according to bandwidth, reuse, and SLOs.
approach_1aa1ad25-f3d9-4369-ae7f-7eaad31.name: Serving memory management, KV reuse, and hierarchy

approach_95517d76-bb4d-44d5-8d01-190178c.core_idea: Reduce how many distinct KV projections and cache tensors a model creates by sharing KV heads within or across layers. This changes the trained architecture and capacity-quality frontier rather than compressing an existing cache at inference time.
approach_95517d76-bb4d-44d5-8d01-190178c.name: Architectural KV head and layer sharing

approach_b566f492-f54c-455b-92ba-42f1e90.core_idea: Reduce bytes per retained KV element with key/value-aware quantization, residual high-precision regions, outlier protection, calibration, and compressed attention kernels; hybrid systems may quantize an already selected subset.
approach_b566f492-f54c-455b-92ba-42f1e90.name: Low-bit numerical KV representation

approach_e93e0d98-1e40-4eb8-8180-374ffcf.core_idea: Reduce cache length by retaining task-, attention-, or semantic-chunk-important tokens plus local/sink context; selection can be fixed after prefill, updated during decode, or allocated unevenly across layers.
approach_e93e0d98-1e40-4eb8-8180-374ffcf.name: Token-selective retention and bounded attention

finding_003bc3f2-acc0-4fd4-a017-1742663c.statement: Deployment boundary is now explicit: H2O, StreamingLLM, SnapKV, XKV, MiniKV, KIVI, KVQuant, PagedAttention, CacheGen, and LMCache operate on existing weights, while CLA/MLKV require pretraining or uptraining and alter the model architecture; the two classes can in principle be layered but need joint evaluation.

finding_0a9941a8-fad3-4216-91c0-a3053727.statement: Hybrid compression is not mechanically composable: MiniKV makes H2O-style persistent selection plus KIVI-style INT2 quantization work through co-designed grouping and kernels, yet substituting SnapKV selection causes a reported LongBench drop from about 35 to 32 because selected tokens differ in quantization sensitivity.

finding_11d0945f-925e-45a7-af77-b6828fa2.statement: Irreversible token eviction trades global recall for bounded compute and memory: heavy-hitter-plus-recency and pooled prompt clusters outperform naive windows/top-k in tested workloads, but content outside the retained cache cannot be recovered and task-dependent saliency remains a quality boundary.

finding_1c70dddf-5bb4-4683-bf28-29423c60.statement: Independent benchmarks show that cache quality is task-, model-, prompt-, budget-, and generation-regime-dependent: arithmetic, code, safety, and long self-generated reasoning can degrade far more than retrieval or knowledge tasks, and aggressive eviction may lengthen or prevent termination of reasoning traces.

finding_55db5f0f-20a3-4cdb-9027-1ce3add4.statement: Published memory and speedup numbers are corpus-, model-, kernel-, hardware-, batch-, and baseline-dependent: H2O gains partly come from larger batches or avoiding offload, SnapKV fixes prompt-cache size, KIVI increases batch capacity, and CacheGen assumes cache reuse over constrained networks; direct scalar ranking would be invalid.

finding_76db67d8-c1cc-4c8a-9cd6-95f69b08.statement: Layer-adaptive allocation is a policy dimension inside token selection rather than a separate compression primitive: XKV calibrates application-specific per-layer budgets, whereas MiniKV's pyramid policy combines layer allocation with persistent-token selection and INT2 representation.

finding_81c0bc55-3b07-4a05-ab88-5e86598d.statement: Serving memory management reduces a different cost than lossy compression: PagedAttention removes reservation/fragmentation and enables exact prefix sharing inside GPU memory, LMCache extends exact reuse and movement across storage tiers, and CacheGen reduces bytes transferred when cross-machine bandwidth is the bottleneck.

finding_ad1e6ce0-ceac-4cac-b7ea-7e050081.statement: Architectural sharing is a distinct training-time route: CLA and MLKV reduce the layer dimension of the cache and compose with MQA/GQA head sharing, but unchanged per-layer cache reads mean capacity reduction alone does not guarantee decode latency or throughput gains.

finding_b1c2d6c8-6dec-4477-8b9b-25f2d33d.statement: The literature disagrees on whether reasoning-tuned models are intrinsically more robust: KVFundaBench reports stronger averaged robustness for one distilled reasoning model, while long-generation evaluation finds most eviction methods still substantially trail full cache; the difference follows task mix, output horizon, budget, and eviction policy rather than a universal model property.

finding_b96a21d5-724d-4d2c-97c3-f5913ce3.statement: Token reduction is not one mechanism: H2O updates importance during decode from accumulated attention, SnapKV chooses prompt positions once after prefill using an observation window, and StreamingLLM keeps sinks plus recent tokens for bounded streaming; their guarantees and failure modes are therefore not interchangeable.

finding_c0997616-7ed2-4469-ab34-d21b53a6.statement: Exact reuse/offload gains are conditional: paged allocation helps most when serving is memory-bound, while lower-tier loading helps only with sufficient reuse and when transfer beats recomputation; LMCache's reported crossover moves with bandwidth and context length.

finding_d1d3680d-cb20-45d8-96af-120905bc.statement: Evidence for cross-layer sharing is not uniform: natively pretrained CLA2 improves the tested accuracy-memory Pareto frontier at 1B/3B scale, whereas uptrained 160M/410M MLKV generally underperforms MQA/GQA at equal KV-head count and extreme sharing becomes unusable.

finding_df730fa1-d5c8-4cd0-9f3f-b8a96e40.statement: KIVI and KVQuant independently agree that keys and values require different low-bit treatment, but they make different engineering choices: KIVI uses grouped per-channel keys and a full-precision recent residual, whereas KVQuant uses calibrated pre-RoPE keys, sparse outliers, and attention-sink protection.

finding_f497cf3d-eeeb-4743-9ce5-7bbf873b.statement: KV cache pressure is multidimensional: sequence length and batch concurrency enlarge resident memory and bandwidth demand, while reuse across machines adds a separate transfer/TTFT bottleneck; reducing one cost does not automatically reduce the others.

finding_fa536ddc-f100-4852-9647-5842b24b.statement: Several routes are composable because they reduce different dimensions: H2O reports compatibility with quantization, KVQuant combines with weight quantization, and CacheGen further encodes token-pruned caches for transfer; composition still needs joint quality and end-to-end system evaluation.

problem_5e452a59-92ab-40b4-a3ee-aa20e646.statement: How can a bounded cache adapt to saliency shifts across prefill and long generation, preserve semantic chunks and distant evidence, and avoid the longer or nonterminating reasoning traces observed under aggressive eviction?

problem_825e2348-0d0e-4d50-bab3-5a01be79.statement: Can architectural KV sharing be validated on modern large long-context models with end-to-end kernels and serving workloads, and then combined with inference-time quantization or selection without compounding quality loss?

problem_99d2a011-e3da-4d8f-81cc-919e2d05.statement: Can extreme low-bit KV formats deliver portable end-to-end gains across attention architectures, prompt processing, reasoning tasks, and hardware without calibration mismatch or bespoke kernel/allocation overhead?

problem_ae7f9575-3621-4b8d-985a-c5fbbbd6.statement: How should a serving controller jointly choose paging, cache encoding, storage tier, prefetch, eviction, and recomputation under changing bandwidth, cache-hit rates, concurrent load, and TTFT/ITL SLOs?

contributions: Enables sub-channel key quantization after eviction by selecting a persistent heavy-hitter set at the end of prefill.
Combines medium-rate token eviction with 2-bit KV quantization and optional pyramid layer allocation.
Adds a two-pass selective FlashAttention-style prefill kernel and fused decode dequantization to keep auxiliary memory linear.
key_results: On LongBench with Llama-2 and Mistral models, MiniKV-Pyramid reaches 98.5% of full-model average for Llama-2-7B at a 0.33 GB cache in the stated 4096-prompt/512-generation comparison.
Long-context experiments show high eviction rates can fail; GSM8K requires roughly a 90% adaptive token budget to match full-cache reasoning accuracy.

System tests on one A100 show lower peak memory and higher throughput, but the selective prefill kernel is slower than FlashAttention in the reported microbenchmark while enabling attention-score collection without quadratic materialization.
limitations: Persistent heavy hitters are observed mainly at medium budgets; the assumption weakens at tiny budgets and long-context quality drops under aggressive eviction.
LongBench generations are capped below 512 tokens, limiting evidence about long self-generated reasoning.
Composition is not plug-and-play: replacing H2O selection with SnapKV before KIVI drops the reported LongBench score from about 35 to 32.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It directly tests composition between token eviction and numerical compression and shows that successful composition depends on selected-token distributions, cache budget, task, and kernel support.
analysis.summary: MiniKV is an inference-only co-design that combines persistent prefill heavy-hitter selection, a recent window, layer-wise budget allocation, asymmetric INT2 KV quantization, and fused selective-attention/dequantization kernels.

source.title: MiniKV: Pushing the Limits of LLM Inference via 2-Bit Layer-Discriminative KV Cache

contributions: Builds a multi-capability benchmark over four model variants and six eviction methods rather than only long-prompt retrieval.
Analyzes sink-removed attention distributions to explain why arithmetic reasoning depends on a broader set of non-sink tokens.
Introduces separate prefill/decode compression that preserves whole high-scoring shots as semantic chunks.
key_results: Tasks are mostly stable above a 40% retained ratio, but arithmetic, code, and safety drop sharply under more aggressive compression; sensitivity also varies by model type and prompt shot count.
On LG-GSM8K with about 4K generated tokens, StreamingLLM, H2O, and PyramidInfer lose more than 20 percentage points below a 30% retained ratio.
ShotKV retains 47.33% accuracy at 40% versus 46.00% full cache on LG-GSM8K and substantially exceeds the tested unified eviction baselines at 25%-30%, under the paper's setup.
limitations: The benchmark studies eviction methods, not numerical quantization, exact offload, or architecture-changing cache reduction.
Experiments use selected 7B-8B models and one A40 environment, so exact thresholds are not universal.
Its conclusion that a reasoning-tuned model is more robust in averaged tasks differs from studies of self-generated reasoning traces, underscoring benchmark dependence.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It independently demonstrates task-, prompt-, and model-dependent failure thresholds and provides direct long-generation evidence that popular unified eviction policies degrade sharply under aggressive compression.
analysis.summary: KVFundaBench evaluates six fundamental capability categories under token-level KV eviction, including knowledge, arithmetic, commonsense, code, safety, and roughly 4K-token long generation; it also proposes ShotKV to preserve coherent in-context examples.

source.title: Can LLMs Maintain Fundamental Abilities under KV Cache Compression?

contributions: Empirically identifies greater than 95% attention sparsity in most OPT layers and a power-law heavy-hitter distribution.
Defines an online greedy heavy-hitter-plus-recency eviction policy under a fixed cache budget.
Provides a system implementation that avoids memory movement when replacing evicted entries.
key_results: At a 20% cache budget, H2O often matches full-cache quality across OPT, LLaMA, and GPT-NeoX tasks; local-only and fixed sparse baselines can collapse.

On T4 and A100 experiments, reported gains include up to 5x memory reduction without measured accuracy loss, up to 3x throughput over FlexGen, and 1.1-1.9x latency reduction at matched batch size; comparisons use specific model, sequence, offloading, and hardware settings.
The paper reports compatibility with KV quantization and shows that neither heavy hitters nor recent tokens alone match the combined policy on all tested tasks.
limitations: Eviction is irreversible and local accumulated attention is only a proxy for future importance.
The theoretical guarantee assumes a submodular attention objective; empirical speedups depend on batch size, offloading regime, hardware, and baseline.
The four-million-token demonstration emphasizes perplexity and limited samples rather than general long-range retrieval.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It establishes the decode-time token-importance route and shows how memory reduction can translate into larger batches, less offloading, and higher throughput, while exposing irreversible-eviction risk.
analysis.summary: H2O is an inference-only, fixed-budget KV eviction policy. It uses online accumulated attention scores to retain heavy-hitter tokens and combines them with recent tokens, avoiding a future-aware offline policy.

source.title: H$_2$O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models

contributions: Identifies low-bandwidth cross-machine KV fetching as a bottleneck distinct from local GPU capacity.
Exploits token locality and heterogeneous layer sensitivity to encode independently decodable cache chunks.
Selects encoding level or text recomputation online as bandwidth changes while keeping multiple representations offline.
key_results: Across Mistral-7B, Llama-34B/70B and four datasets on A40 servers at 3 Gbps, CacheGen reports 3.1-4.7x lower TTFT than fetching text and 3.2-3.7x lower TTFT than default quantization.
Encoded transfer size falls 3.5-4.3x relative to the quantization baseline with reported degradation no more than 2% accuracy, 0.1% F1, or 0.1 perplexity in the tested settings.
Encoding H2O/LLMLingua-compressed caches yields a further 3.3-4.2x transfer reduction, but the H2O offline experiment is explicitly idealized.
limitations: Benefits shrink above roughly 20 Gbps and depend on reuse across machines; this is not a generic decode-memory result.
Multiple encoded versions add offline complexity, and the default 1.5K chunk size is empirically chosen.
If bandwidth forces low-quality encodings for most chunks, output quality still degrades; adaptation reacts one chunk late.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It separates transmission footprint and transfer delay from resident GPU cache memory, and directly demonstrates composition with token pruning.
analysis.summary: CacheGen targets KV reuse across machines: it converts cache tensors into compact bitstreams using token-delta encoding, layer-sensitive quantization, and channel/layer arithmetic coding, then adapts chunk encoding or text recomputation to observed network bandwidth and a TTFT SLO.

source.title: CacheGen: KV Cache Compression and Streaming for Fast Large Language Model Serving

contributions: Formalizes Dynamic Differences of Importance Distribution across layers and links a retained-information proxy to final accuracy.
Uses a lightweight no-cache mini-prefill plus greedy optimization to assign layer-specific capacities under an accuracy constraint.
Amortizes allocation by sampling application tasks in advance rather than recalibrating every request.
key_results: Across 14 LongBench datasets on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and one RTX A6000, XKV reports 61.6% average KV memory reduction, at least 12.8 percentage points more than the best tested competitor under its accuracy bounds.
On NarrativeQA, cache memory falls from 4.00 GB to 1.54 GB, per-task time from 7.18 s to 3.40 s, and maximum batch size rises from 8 to 20; reported throughput improves up to 5.2x.
At extremely low 1.2%-1.6% retained ratios, all methods lose accuracy, while XKV is best on most of the reported datasets rather than lossless.
limitations: Allocation depends on application-specific samples and statistics collected with a lightweight proxy model, so distribution shift can invalidate the budget.
Evaluation is limited to one model family, one GPU type, and selected LongBench tasks.
The method changes allocation across layers but still inherits irreversible token-eviction failure modes.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It shows that layer-adaptive budget allocation is a policy within token-selective retention, not a separate representation mechanism; it also exposes application sampling and proxy-model overhead.
analysis.summary: XKV is an inference-only token-eviction method that measures application-specific, layer-varying importance distributions, then uses a lightweight mini-prefill and greedy optimization to allocate different cache budgets across layers.

source.title: XKV: Personalized KV Cache Memory Reduction for Long-Context LLM Inference

contributions: Introduces an attention kernel that follows block tables over non-contiguous KV storage.
Applies virtual-memory ideas to dynamic block allocation, prompt/beam copy-on-write sharing, swapping, and recomputation.
Integrates paged cache management with continuous batching and distributed tensor-parallel execution.
key_results: The paper reports effective memory utilization as low as 20.4% for contiguous preallocation baselines, while PagedAttention limits per-request waste to the final block.
On A100 OPT/LLaMA serving traces, vLLM sustains 1.7-2.7x higher request rates than the infeasible Orca oracle and 2.7-8x over maximum reservation at comparable latency.
Copy-on-write sharing saves 37.6-55.2% cache memory for beam search on the reported Alpaca setting and raises shared-prefix throughput up to 3.58x.
limitations: Indirection and non-contiguous access require a custom fused attention kernel and introduce overhead.
Benefits shrink when workloads are compute-bound, such as short sequences with abundant memory.
Preemption uses coarse sequence-level eviction and must choose between CPU swapping and recomputation based on platform bandwidth and compute.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It establishes serving-time memory management as a route separate from lossy tensor compression: it improves usable capacity, batching, and sharing without changing model quality.
analysis.summary: PagedAttention/vLLM separates logical KV blocks from non-contiguous physical GPU blocks, allocating them on demand and using copy-on-write sharing for prompts and beam branches. It preserves exact KV values while reducing reservation and fragmentation waste.

source.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

contributions: Separates pre-RoPE key and per-token value quantization to preserve channel structure.
Uses offline sensitivity-weighted calibration and per-vector dense-and-sparse outlier handling.
Protects the first attention-sink token and supplies fused GPU kernels for compressed matvec operations.
key_results: On calibrated LLaMA-family Wikitext-2 tests, 4/3/2-bit configurations with 1% sparse outliers report 3.7/4.8/6.9x memory savings with under 0.02/0.1/0.5 perplexity degradation.
For LLaMA-2-7B-32K, 3-bit KVQuant is materially stronger than similar-bit KIVI on RULER, while 2-bit performance still drops on harder multi-key tasks.
A6000 batch-1 kernels report roughly 1.2-1.7x key/value matvec latency savings; the 1M/10M-context claims are enabled capacity configurations, not universal task-quality demonstrations.
limitations: Non-uniform formats and key scaling rely on calibration data; value statistics still require online work.
Latency evaluation focuses on memory-bandwidth-bound decode rather than prompt processing.
The end-to-end sparse-cache update path still copies old data during concatenation and requires allocation optimization.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It extends the quantization route beyond uniform low-bit storage and exposes calibration, outlier, positional-encoding, kernel, and prefill trade-offs.
analysis.summary: KVQuant combines pre-RoPE per-channel key quantization, per-token value quantization, calibration-derived non-uniform datatypes, per-vector sparse outlier retention, and attention-sink protection. It uses custom kernels to dequantize and apply RoPE during attention.

source.title: KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization

contributions: Measures fixed key-channel outliers and shows per-channel key quantization yields much lower attention-score error.
Shows sparse attention makes per-token value quantization substantially safer than per-channel value quantization.
Adds a streaming residual-buffer design and hardware-aware mixed-precision kernels without finetuning.
key_results: KIVI-2 stays within roughly 2% accuracy of fp16 on tested Llama/Mistral generation tasks and remains close on selected LongBench tasks; Falcon's already compressed MQA cache often needs 4-bit precision.
On a single A100-80GB with Llama-2-7B ShareGPT-like workloads, the smaller cache permits up to 4x larger batches and reports 2.35-3.47x throughput.
GSM8K ablations show aggressive quantization without a suitable full-precision residual window can sharply degrade reasoning quality.
limitations: Quality depends on model attention architecture, group size, task, and the full-precision residual window.
Benefits require specialized Triton/CUDA kernels; low bits alone do not guarantee end-to-end speedup.
Reported throughput uses a specific A100 workload and is partly enabled by increasing batch size rather than lowering every request's latency.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It grounds low-bit numerical compression, the different error geometry of keys and values, and the quality role of a full-precision recency window.
analysis.summary: KIVI is a tuning-free asymmetric KV quantizer: keys use group-wise per-channel 2-bit quantization, values use per-token quantization, and a small recent residual cache stays in full precision. Custom GPU kernels fuse dequantization with attention operations.

source.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache

contributions: Identifies attention sinks as a softmax-induced dependence on initial tokens rather than their semantics.
Combines four initial sink tokens with a rolling recent-token cache and cache-relative positional handling.
Demonstrates both a tuning-free deployment path and a trained learnable-sink alternative.
key_results: Across Llama-2, MPT, Pythia, and Falcon, PG19 perplexity remains stable over streams up to four million tokens with fixed cache sizes.
On A6000 tests against sliding-window recomputation, per-token decoding speedup reaches up to 22.2x while using a comparable cache footprint.
LongBench shows a 4+3496 sink/recent cache underperforms a 1750+1750 truncation baseline; performance recovers when task-relevant initial content is retained.
limitations: It only uses information currently in the sink-plus-recent cache and does not turn a short-context model into a full long-range retrieval model.
Stable perplexity on a stream is not equivalent to remembering distant facts; StreamEval deliberately asks about recent information.
Cache-size increases do not monotonically improve perplexity, suggesting models may underuse available context.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It separates bounded-cache streaming stability from general long-context retrieval and shows why naive sliding-window eviction can fail catastrophically.
analysis.summary: StreamingLLM keeps a few initial attention-sink tokens plus a rolling window of recent tokens and reindexes positions inside the cache. Existing RoPE/ALiBi models need no finetuning; a separately trained sink-token model is an architectural variant.

source.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks

contributions: Defines configurable KV sharing across consecutive transformer layers and explains its composition with MHA, GQA, and MQA.
Maps sharing factor to cache reduction while identifying pipeline-parallel communication constraints and unchanged core-attention bandwidth.
Trains 1B- and 3B-parameter models from scratch to compare accuracy-memory Pareto frontiers.
key_results: CLA reduces KV cache memory approximately by its sharing factor; MQA-CLA2 halves cache bytes per token relative to the matched-head MQA model.
At 1B and 3B scales, MQA-CLA2 is within less than 1% perplexity change of matched-head MQA in the tested regimes and improves the Pareto frontier relative to shrinking head dimension alone.
Sharing factors above two and non-uniform dense-front/back patterns produce worse accuracy-memory trade-offs than uniform CLA2 in the reported ablations.
limitations: The evidence is from models trained from scratch at 1B and 3B parameters with 2K training sequences, not retrofits to production long-context models.
End-to-end long-context serving latency and throughput are explicitly left for future work.
Shared KV must still be reread at every consuming layer, so cache capacity falls without a direct reduction in core attention bandwidth or latency.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It establishes cross-layer sharing as a mechanism distinct from inference-only eviction or quantization: it reduces the number of layer-specific KV tensors, but does not directly reduce the attention kernel's per-layer reads.
analysis.summary: Cross-Layer Attention (CLA) is a model-architecture intervention that computes KV projections in only a subset of layers and reuses those activations in adjacent layers. Its sharing factor is orthogonal to MHA, GQA, and MQA and requires native model training.

source.title: Reducing Transformer Key-Value Cache Size with Cross-Layer Attention

contributions: Generalizes MQA/GQA sharing from heads within a layer to KV heads shared among groups of layers.
Derives cache size as proportional to the number of KV-producing layer groups and KV head groups.
Measures accuracy, memory scaling, maximum batch size, and throughput after model uptraining.
key_results: Memory scales linearly with the chosen total KV head count; in the small-model setup, the baseline reaches batch 48 while extreme MLKV variants reach batches around 940-1100.
MLKV generally underperforms GQA or MQA at the same KV-head count, and MLKV-1 degrades severely; moderate MLKV-6/12 settings offer the better measured trade-offs.
The generalized implementation shows no significant throughput speedup because shared cache contents are still fetched at every layer.
limitations: Experiments cover only decoder-only 160M and 410M models, with limited downstream task diversity.
Models are uptrained rather than pretrained natively with MLKV, leaving training-procedure effects unresolved.
No optimized kernel demonstrates that the large capacity gains translate to per-token latency or throughput gains.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It independently supports the architectural cross-layer-sharing route while supplying a cautionary counterpoint: theoretical cache savings do not automatically improve throughput or preserve quality.
analysis.summary: MLKV shares KV heads both within and across layers, reducing the layer dimension from all layers to a smaller number of KV-producing layer groups. The paper applies the design by uptraining small Pythia models rather than using an inference-only transformation.

source.title: MLKV: Multi-Layer Key-Value Heads for Memory Efficient Transformer Decoding

contributions: Benchmarks H2O, StreamingLLM, KNorm, R-KV, a decoding-updated SnapKV variant, and ShadowKV over 128-512 token budgets.
Separates non-reasoning and reasoning models across reading, logic, commonsense, and math tasks with up to 2048 generated tokens.
Relates accuracy to attention loss and measures the hidden effect of compression on generation length and throughput.
key_results: Very small budgets cause large and method-dependent accuracy collapses; on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B GSM8K, H2O rises from 0.21 at budget 128 to 0.52 at 512, while full cache is 0.70.
Attention-based H2O and the decoding SnapKV variant dominate other eviction heuristics on reasoning models, but usually still trail full cache; no one method dominates the non-reasoning model.
Aggressive eviction can produce longer or circular reasoning traces, so nominal memory savings can increase total inference compute and fail to terminate.
limitations: The study covers token eviction rather than low-bit quantization or architecture changes.
Its SnapKV-D variant periodically updates during decode and is not the original fixed-prefill SnapKV algorithm.
Most dataset results use 100 examples per seed and a 2048-output cap on a specific A6000/kvpress implementation.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It supplies missing evidence that quality under compression cannot be inferred from prompt-only long-context tests: micro-budgets can collapse reasoning, lengthen output, and even induce nontermination.
analysis.summary: Hold Onto That Thought independently evaluates token-eviction strategies on long generated reasoning traces across conventional and reasoning-tuned 7B-14B models, multiple reasoning categories, and fixed cache budgets.

source.title: Hold Onto That Thought: Assessing KV Cache Compression On Reasoning

contributions: Shows that prompt attention patterns visible near the end of prefill are often stable during the measured generation interval.
Introduces per-head top-k voting plus pooling to preserve contextual clusters rather than isolated high-score tokens.
Maintains constant prompt KV size during decode and requires no model training.
key_results: On one A100-80GB with LWM-Text-Chat-1M, a 1024-token prompt cache retrieves needles through 140K with little loss and can run inputs up to 380K where the baseline OOMs at 33K.
At 16K input and batch size 2, reported decode latency falls from over 100 ms/token to below 40 ms/token, about 3.6x, under the paper's implementation and hardware.
Across four LongBench model families with roughly 13K average input, 1024-token caches give about 92% prompt-cache compression but some summarization and synthetic tasks still degrade.
limitations: Important positions vary with the instruction, so static importance independent of the current prompt is unreliable.
The selected prompt cache is not updated during generation; later saliency shifts can invalidate early selection.
Quality depends on observation-window, pooling, cache-capacity, task, and base-model choices; compression ratios are not universal.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It represents prompt-aware, pre-generation token selection and provides a mechanistic contrast with H2O's decode-time updates and StreamingLLM's fixed recency window.
analysis.summary: SnapKV performs inference-only prompt-cache compression before generation. Queries in the prompt's final observation window vote per attention head for important prefix positions; pooling keeps neighboring token clusters and the observation window is retained in full.

source.title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation

contributions: Defines a standardized connector and token-indexed cache layer across vLLM/SGLang and heterogeneous backends.
Batches small pages into larger chunks, pipelines layer loads, prefetches queued requests, and supports dynamic offloading with minimal copies.
Evaluates CPU offload, remote centralized storage, real traces, and prefill/decode disaggregation.
key_results: On H100 serving setups, LMCache reports 1.9-8.1x lower TTFT and 2.3-14x higher throughput than its strongest tested baseline in single-node offload workloads, with model- and load-specific conditions.
Remote centralized storage improves throughput 1.3-3x in the tested 15 Gbps setup, and chunked CPU loading reaches 400 Gbps versus 88 Gbps for native vLLM offload.
At 32 Gbps on B200, loading beats recomputation only beyond roughly 256K input tokens; at 64/128 Gbps it wins across tested lengths.
limitations: Benefits require cache reuse and sufficient lower-tier capacity; cold or low-hit workloads do not avoid prefill.
The load-versus-recompute crossover is bandwidth-, model-, and context-dependent, so static offloading can hurt latency.
Several baselines and production lessons are version- or deployment-specific, including black-box commercial comparisons and a 500 GB CPU-cache budget.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It expands the memory-hierarchy route beyond encoded transfer: the cache values stay exact, while capacity, hit rate, transfer granularity, and compute-I/O overlap determine TTFT and throughput.
analysis.summary: LMCache is a serving-layer system for exact KV reuse across GPU, CPU, disk, remote, and disaggregated prefill/decode tiers. It groups paged caches into transfer chunks, overlaps layer-wise I/O with compute, prefetches asynchronously, and minimizes duplicate copies.

source.title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference

contributions: States a fixed-capacity KV design goal and a dynamic cache update mechanism.
Reports a 1B-parameter experiment intended to compare memory, speed, and BLEU after the 2048-token capacity is reached.
key_results: The paper claims constant memory and relatively constant inference speed beyond a 2048-token capacity.
It reports BLEU as comparable to a traditional cache, but the accessible result is incomplete and lacks enough detail for a reliable effect-size comparison.
limitations: The accessible source does not specify the dynamic-update algorithm at reproducible depth.
Baseline configuration, task construction, complete numerical results, and quality evaluation are insufficiently reported.
The evidence should not be used as a representative primary basis for a major route.
analysis.relevance_to_run: It is a candidate trained bounded-state route, but the accessible primary source is too underspecified to support route-level generalization or quantitative comparison.
analysis.summary: This paper proposes a Transformer with a predefined 2048-token KV capacity and a dynamic update mechanism intended to keep memory and inference time constant beyond that length.

source.title: A Method for Building Large Language Models with Predefined KV Cache Capacity
